'''Yulia Sister''' ({{langx|he|יוליה סיסטר}}, {{langx|ru|Юлия Давидовна Систер}}; born September 12, 1936, in [[Chișinău]], [[Bessarabia]], [[Kingdom of Romania|Romania]]) is a [[USSR|Soviet]] [[Moldavian SSR|Moldavian]] and [[Israel]]i [[Analytical chemistry|analytical chemist]] engaged in chemical research with the use of [[polarography]] and [[chromatography]], a science historian, and a researcher of Russian Jewry in Israel, France, and other countries. She holds the position of Director General of the Research Centre for Russian Jews abroad and in Israel.<ref name="nizi">{{cite web|url=http://nizi.co.il/author/yuliya-sister|title=Our Authors: Yulia Sister|publisher=Internet magazine "Science and Life Israel"|access-date=15 July 2015|archive-date=17 July 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150717121952/http://nizi.co.il/author/yuliya-sister|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="sciencerehovot">{{cite book |url=http://rehes.org/he/lst1_files/Biographies.doc |title=Who Are the Members of the House of Scientists and Experts of Rehovot |publisher=[[Ministry of Immigrant Absorption]]|year=2008}}</ref><ref name="nnedeli">{{cite journal  |title=Dr. Julia Sister: chemist, popularizer of science, publicist|author=Prof. Aron Cherniak|journal=Novosti Nedeli, Evreiskii Kamerton Supplement|language=ru|pages=16|year=2006}}</ref><ref name="newswe092008">{{cite web|author=Leonid Shkolnik|url=http://newswe.com/index.php?go=Pages&in=view&id=625|title=That's us: September 12‒18, 2008|publisher=Online newspaper at NewsWe.com|date=September 2008|language=ru|access-date=15 July 2015}}</ref><ref name="madan">{{cite web|author1=Nikolai Borschevsky |author2=Dan Haruv |author3=Konstantin Kikoin |author4=Mikhail Parkhomovsky |url=http://madan.org.il/node/10037|title=To the anniversary of Yulia Sister|publisher=Madan.org.il|access-date=15 July 2015}}</ref>

==Biography==

===Early childhood and schools===
Yulia Sister was born in 1936 in Chișinău ([[Russian language|Russian]]:  Kishinev), at the time in the Kingdom of Romania, a city which later became the capital of the [[Moldavian Soviet Socialist Republic|Moldavian SSR]] and since 1991 is the capital of [[Moldova]]. Her parents and paternal grandparents were also born in this city. The grandparents were there and survived the [[Chișinău pogrom (1903)|pogrom of 1903]].<ref name="nnedeli"/><ref name="rehes11112010">{{cite web|author=Bella Kerdman|url=http://rehes.org/rus_iud/lst1_3u.html|title=Mrs. Director General|publisher=Novosti Nedeli, Evreiskii Kamerton Supplement|date=11 November 2010|language=ru|access-date=15 July 2015}}</ref>

David Iosifovich, Yulia's father, was a doctor educated in [[Prague]] at [[Charles University in Prague|Charles University]]. He used to tell his daughter about his student years, the [[Bessarabia]]n association of fellow-countrymen in Prague and his meetings with famous people. Yulia's mother Yevgenia (Bathsheba) Moiseevna copied for her by hand children's verses and Yulia learned to read quite early. Among the first poems was "What Is Good and What Is Bad" by [[Mayakovsky]].<ref name="rehes11112010"/><ref name="libru">{{cite web|author=Yulia Sister|url=http://world.lib.ru/s/sister_j_d/devochkavstepi.shtml|title=Girl on the Steppe|publisher=[[Lib.ru]]|date=August 2013|language=ru|access-date=15 July 2015}}</ref>

Yulia's grandparents stuck to traditions and spoke [[Yiddish]], and grandfather Yosef (Iosif) even wrote Yiddish poetry. But Yulia could hardly remember them. Her grandfather Moshe (Moisei) died before she was born; her parental grandparents lost their lives in the [[Kishinev Ghetto]] in the [[Holocaust]] and her grandmother Sarah died during the [[World War II]] in evacuation.<ref name="rehes11112010"/><ref name="dorledor">{{cite web|author=Miriam Landau|url=http://www.dorledor.info/node/8705|title=Fellow countrymen: Yulia, selfmadewoman|publisher=Portal Dorledor|date=28 March 2008|language=ru|access-date=15 July 2015}}</ref>

During the 2nd World War Bessarabia was reclaimed and then [[Soviet occupation of Bessarabia and Northern Bukovina|occupied by the Soviet Union]] in June 1940. A year later in July 1941 it was reconquered by Germany and Romania, and in August 1944 reoccupied by the Soviet Union.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.jewishvirtuallibrary.org/jsource/vjw/moldova.html#20|title=Moldova|publisher=[[Jewishvirtuallibrary.org]]|access-date=15 July 2015}}</ref> In her memoirs Yulia recalled the day when the [[Red Army]] entered Kishinev. She also remembered the German bombing of the city and the air raids on the roads, by which her family escaped to the East from the Nazis.<ref name="libru"/>

At the beginning of the war David Sister and his family was evacuated to the left bank of the [[Volga River]] where he was appointed chief physician at the district hospital and a consultant of the nearby military hospital. The hospital was located in the open [[steppe]] between two villages and on the other side of Volga there was [[Stalingrad]]. The family lived there a few years. There were no other children in the neighborhood and Yulia had no friends to play with. But she was fascinated by the local nature and made observations of plants and animals. The inhabitants of the hospital could hear the cannonade from the other bank, and during the [[battle of Stalingrad]] it became particularly strong.<ref name="rehes11112010"/><ref name="libru"/>

In 1944 Yulia's family moved to [[Kropyvnytskyi|Kirovograd]] where she, after a year's delay, was enrolled in the first grade of primary education. A year later the family came back to the native city of Kishinev. Despite severe post-war shortages and difficulties, the Sister's family succeeded to restore their home, which included a huge library. Among the family friends and guests were writers, actors, musicians and scientists, and Yulia grew up in an atmosphere of thirst for knowledge.<ref name="rehes11112010"/>

Between the years of 1945 and 1954 Yulia Sister studied at the School for Girls Number 2 in Kishinev. Chemistry was taught very passionately by a teacher that loved the subject and was able to convey her enthusiasm to the students. On the advice of her teacher Sister participated in the chemistry enrichment program for school children that was carried out by Professor {{Interlanguage link multi|Anton Ablov|ro}} at the [[Moldova State University|University of Kishinev]].<ref name="dorledor"/>

===Education and research career===

Yulia Sister entered the Department of Chemistry of the University of Kishinev in the fall 1954. While asked by Professor {{Interlanguage link multi|Iurie Lealicov|ro|3=Yuri Lyalikov}}, who interviewed the applicants to the Department, why she has chosen this Department, she explained that thanks to her school teacher she fell in love with chemistry. At the University Yulia was involved in various campus activities, and served as an editor of the faculty newspaper "Chemist".<ref name="rehes092010">{{cite web|author=Yulia Sister|url=http://www.rehes.org/lst2/lst2_83.html|title=Academician Yuri Sergeyevich Lyalikov|publisher=The House of Scientists and Experts of Rehovot|date=September 2010|language=ru|access-date=15 July 2015}}</ref> Since her second year at the university she became a member of the student scientific society and was engaged in the research of compounds called [[heteropolyacid]]s.<ref name="dorledor"/> In 1959 Sister successfully defended her Master's thesis "Precipitation chromatography of heteropolyacids." and graduated with honors from the University of Kishinev.<ref name="nizi"/>

Upon completion of the studies Sister was assigned to the laboratory of analytical chemistry headed by Professor Yuri Lyalikov.<ref name="dorledor"/> The laboratory was a part of the Institute of Chemistry at the Moldavian branch of the [[Academy of Sciences of the USSR]], which became the [[Academy of Sciences of Moldova]] in 1961. Working in this laboratory allowed the young chemist Sister to begin her research with new [[Polarography|polarographic methods]]. In order to carry out analysis of organic compounds by the means of alternating-current (ac) polarography Yulia built with her own hands a polarograph and received the first polarograms. Sister was the first in Moldova (with Y. S. Lyalikov), who applied the methods of ac polarography and second harmonic ac polarography for analyzing organic compounds. Then, together with the physicist Vil Senkevich, they assembled an automatic device, and only later began the serial production of polarographs in the USSR. In the early 1960s Yulia published her first research articles. In 1967 she received her Ph.D. from the Institute of Chemistry of the Moldavian Academy of Sciences.<ref name="nizi"/><ref name="newswe092008"/><ref name="rehes102014">{{cite web|author=Yulia Sister|url=http://rehes.org/rus_iud/s_seminar60.html|title=Academician Y. S. Lyalikov School of polarography in Kishinev|publisher=The House of Scientists and Experts of Rehovot|date=October 2014|language=ru|access-date=15 July 2015}}</ref>

Through 25 years of research at the Institute of Chemistry Sister dealt with a wide range of topics. Her [[ecology]] oriented research included analysis of [[pesticides]] in environmental samples, food items and biological mediums. She participated in research and analysis of [[Suspension (chemistry)|suspensions]] and was involved in analyzing new organic compounds. Sister made a substantial contribution to the development of such methods as the second harmonic ac polarography, the difference polarography with magnetic recording, the chromatopolarography. For about 20 years Yulia Sister served as a consultant on the use of the polarographic method in biology at the Department of Human and Animal Physiology of the University of Kishinev.<ref name="nizi"/><ref name="newswe092008"/><ref name="rehes102014"/>

In 1984 Yulia Sister was invited to work with the Institute of Technology and Development where she soon headed the laboratory of physical and chemical methods. The Institute was affiliated to a research and production association in the [[Ialoveni]] (formerly Kutuzov). Sister and her laboratory were using a variety of research methods and among them the [[high-performance liquid chromatography]] being at that time a new approach in the laboratories of the country. She also contributed as a board member of Moldavian branch of the Mendeleev Chemical Society and led the program "Young Chemist" in the Moldavian Republic. Many of her students, the former young chemists, became later scientists and managers of respectable companies.<ref name="nizi"/><ref name="dorledor"/>

===New activities and challenges===

Yulia Sister and her family repatriated to Israel in 1990. In 1992–1993 she served as a senior researcher of the Department of Inorganic and Analytical Chemistry at the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]], and then she was engaged in the topics related to the analysis of biological objects at the [[Tel Aviv University]]. During these years, along with her career in chemistry, Yulia Sister became deeply interested in the study of Russian-Jewish culture.<ref name="nizi"/><ref name="nnedeli"/><ref>{{cite book|editor1-last=Parkhomovsky|editor1-first=Mikhail|editor2-last=Gouzevitch|editor2-first=Dmitri|series=Russian Jewry Abroad|volume=8|title=Pyccкие евреи во Франции. Книга 1|trans-title=Russian Jews in France. Book 1|language=ru|chapter-url=https://archive.org/details/russkoeevrestvov0000unse/page/498|publisher=Research Centre for Russian Jewry Abroad|year=2001|pages=[https://archive.org/details/russkoeevrestvov0000unse/page/498 498–499]|chapter=Yulia Davidovna Sister|isbn=965-222-911-3}}</ref>

In 1991 Sister began to write for the [[Shorter Jewish Encyclopedia]] (SJE) as a non-staff editor. She served as a research fellow covering the field of history of science and wrote about 90 articles for the encyclopedia. Yulia is the author of the articles "Chemistry" (jointly with P. Smorodnitsky), "[[Veniamin Levich]]", "[[Frederick Reines]]", "Moise Haissinsky", "[[Yuri Golfand]]" and many others.<ref name="nizi"/><ref name="rehes11112010"/><ref>{{cite book |editor1-last=Prat|editor1-first=Naftali|editor2-last=Kipnis|editor2-first=Mark|volume=11|script-title=ru:Краткая еврейская энциклопедия|trans-title=Shorter Jewish Encyclopedia|language=ru|publisher=The Society for Research of Jewish Communities|year=2005|pages=889–900|chapter=List of the main articles by authors|isbn=965-320-753-9}}</ref><ref>{{in lang|ru}} [https://eleven.co.il/article/14526 Chemistry], [https://eleven.co.il/article/12394 Veniamin Levich], [https://eleven.co.il/article/13412 Frederick Reines], [https://eleven.co.il/article/11014 Moise Haissinsky], [https://eleven.co.il/article/11255 Yuri Golfand] in EJE ‒ online version of the SJE</ref>

Yulia Sister's activities in the House of Scientists and Experts of [[Rehovot]] started in 1991. Within this forum she organizes lectures, seminars and scientific conferences. She leads the scientific seminars of the House of Scientists that are regularly held at the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]].<ref name="newswe092011">{{cite web|author=Leonid Shkolnik|url=http://www.newswe.com/index.php?go=Pages&in=view&id=4019|title=That's us: September 8‒14, 2011|publisher=Online newspaper at NewsWe.com|date=September 2011|language=ru|access-date=15 July 2015}}</ref> In 2008, and then in 2014 she organized conferences devoted to the [[Bilu (movement)|Bilu]] movement and to the [[First Aliyah]].<ref>{{cite web|author=Yulia Sister|url=http://www.newswe.com/index.php?go=Pages&in=view&id=146|title=Bilu pioneers were the first|publisher=Online newspaper at NewsWe.com|date=28 February 2008|language=ru|access-date=15 July 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|author=Yulia Sister|url=http://rehes.org/rus_iud/konf17122014.html|title=Israel conference devoted to the 130th anniversary of Gedera founded by Bilu pioneers|publisher=The House of Scientists and Experts of Rehovot|date=17 December 2014|language=ru|access-date=15 July 2015}}</ref> She also maintains friendly contacts with foreign colleagues, such as the Club of Russian-speaking scientists of Massachusetts.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://russianscientist.org/files/annarchive/Ubil_zbornic-15-let.pdf|title=Jubilee Almanac|publisher=Massachusetts' Club of Russian-speaking scientists|pages=75–76|date=2011|language=ru|access-date=15 July 2015}}</ref>

In 1997 Mikhail Parkhomovsky initiated creation of the Research Center for Russian Jewry Abroad, which aimed to collect and publish information on Jews, who emigrated from the [[Russian Empire]], [[Soviet Union]] or [[Post-Soviet states]] and made a contribution to world civilization. Parkhomovsky became the Scientific Director and Chief Editor and Yulia Sister Director General of the Center.<ref>{{cite web|author=Leonid Yuniverg|url=http://eholit.ru/news/786/|title=Publishing of Russian books in Israel|publisher=Russian literary echo|date=2011|language=ru|access-date=15 July 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|author=Zeev Green|url=http://newswe.com/index.php?go=Pages&in=view&id=4983|title=Jews, Russia, Israel|publisher=Online newspaper at NewsWe.com|date=13 June 2012|language=ru|access-date=15 July 2015}}</ref> From 2012 the Center changed its name to Research Centre for Russian Jews abroad and in Israel (Erzi).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://eholit.ru/show/centre/erzi/|title=About Research Centre for Russian Jews abroad and in Israel|publisher=Russian literary echo|language=ru|access-date=15 July 2015}}</ref> The collection, processing and publication of materials related to Russian Jewry are organized by Sister. By 2015 the Center published about 30 volumes of collections, including books devoted to Jews in England, France, U.S., Israel and other countries. In addition to her executive functions, Sister is a frequent editor and author of the Center's collective monographs. She is the editor of the 17th volume ("Let Us Build the Walls of Jerusalem. Book 3"), a coeditor of the 11th volume ("Let Us Build the Walls of Jerusalem. Book 1") and of the monograph "Israel, Russian Roots", and a participant in the editing of the 10th volume.<ref name="madan"/><ref name="dorledor"/><ref name="newswe092011"/>

Sister's activities include the organization of seminars and conferences. The following examples are a small sampling of the events organized by the Director General of the Center. In 1999 she was the coordinator of the conference dedicated to the 50th anniversary of the Weizmann Institute in Rehovot. Together with Prof. Aron Cherniak she published a detailed report on the conference and some of its materials in the 8th volume of the "Russian Jewry Abroad" series.<ref name="nnedeli"/><ref name="madan"/> In 2003 Sister led a conference in [[Kiryat Ekron]], in which she introduced the contribution of the Russian [[Aliyah]] to Israeli science, culture and education.<ref>{{cite web|author=Michail Feldman|url=http://aen.ru/index.php?page=brief&article_id=2742|title=Scientific conference in Kiryat Ekron|publisher=Agency for Jewish News (aen.ru)|date=15 September 2003|access-date=15 July 2015|archive-date=17 July 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150717134708/http://aen.ru/index.php?page=brief&article_id=2742|url-status=dead}}</ref> More than 200 scientists from all over the country participated at the tenth-anniversary of the Center conference in 2007.<ref name="dorledor"/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://israel-rehovot.blogspot.co.il/2007/10/conference.html|title=The contribution of scientists from the former Soviet Union is discussed at a conference|publisher=MyRehovot.info|date=31 October 2007|language=ru|access-date=15 July 2015}}</ref> The 2012 conference was devoted to the 130th anniversary of the First Aliyah and the event was covered by the House of Scientists of Rehovot.<ref>{{cite web|author=Yulia Sister|url=http://rehes.org/avtor2/sister_aliy1.html|title=The conference devoted to the 130th anniversary of the First Aliyah|publisher=The House of Scientists and Experts of Rehovot|date=September 2012|language=ru|access-date=15 July 2015}}</ref>

Yulia Sister lives with her family in [[Kiryat Ekron]]. Her husband, Boris (Bezalel) Iosifovich Gendler, is a [[physician]] with an extensive experience in medical practice and education. After his repatriation from Kishinev Bezalel Gendler worked as a doctor in one of the Israeli hospitals and published several articles, some of them in collaboration with Yulia.
